findings.body: `datetime.utcnow()` returns a naive datetime, whereas the previous `datetime.now(UTC)` returned an aware UTC value. Existing code that compares or serializes this field alongside aware datetimes can now fail or lose the UTC offset. Re-import `UTC` and use `datetime.now(UTC)` when restoring the payload return.
findings.failure_scenario: When a caller compares `fetched_at` with an aware UTC datetime, Python raises `TypeError` because the newly returned timestamp is timezone-naive.
findings.title: Keep `fetched_at` timezone-aware

findings.body: The assertion only checks that at least one row remains, so it does not exercise the newly changed behavior that drops the first row. A regression that returns all rows, the wrong row, or a fabricated non-empty result would still pass.
